posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
More blue lasers have entered the market. The newest is a 460nm Coherent saphire laser.

The new semiconductor lasers from Coherent are single mode and TEM00 making them ideal for holography. The most attractive laser for holography so far is the Saphire 480nm at 50mw. 

[http://www.coherent.com/Lasers/index.cf ... howMe=More](http://www.coherent.com/Lasers/index.cfm?fuseaction=show.page&ID=870&loc=834&ShowMe=More)

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md: I wonder what the price will be?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I don't know but I would expect $50,000! As usual we will likely have to wait till they are surplus...

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
And then there are these ones:

[http://www.amazing1.com/blue_lasers.htm](http://www.amazing1.com/blue_lasers.htm)

I wonder who makes them and if they're any good for holography? I've

seen similar looking units elsewhere, but never with price info.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: They have come down in price in the last couple of years. This one is advertised for holography. 100mw for $2500 is not too bad. The Sapphire is SLM, I wonder what the coherence length of the 473nm lasers are. I really don't know what technique they use to get 473nm. They talk about frequency tripling in them but I don't really know the designs.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Oh, OK, If you cool Nd:YAG it will lase at 946nm then doubld we get the 473nm line.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: I phoned the Coherent sales rep in Holland. They gave me a price for the 488-10 sapphire laser. It costs 9000 Euro here.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Heck, 100mw at 473 is PLENTY of power for DCG.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
I looked at the website describing the 100mW 473nm laser. It says it can be used for holography, but for all we know it could be for holography with less than 1mm of depth (i.e., suitable for color holograms of postage stamps). 

If it had a foot of coherence length, the price ($2,149.95) would be a dream come true.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: I imagine someone here could calculate coherence length from linewidth (.01nm) but that is beyone my knowledge. So I e-mailed them and asked them what the coherence length was. I will post if/when they reply.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Less than .01nm is too vague to know. That is a good spec if you are doing chemistry with a laser but we need more accuracy than that. They give those specs so that they represent the worst cases. I would doubt the laser is Single Longitudinal Mode (SLM) or they would have said.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
I think it likely that unless stated otherwise, the too-good-to-be-true cheap blue DPSS lasers are probably not single longitudinal mode (SLM). Multiple modes would cause the notorious contouring (sliced bread) effect in holograms. 

Another blue laser purveyor::

[http://www.crystalaser.com/new/blue.html](http://www.crystalaser.com/new/blue.html)

These guys have a variety of blue DPSS lasers available (and some Q-switched too) , and are much more informative about longitudinal modes. No prices, though. I wonder, since SLM is usually optional, if the S versions are different laser designs or they are just batch selected.
